title: Planar STL boundary extraction and Gmsh 2D generation
overview: Reads one planar STL body loop, reconstructs its boundary, and generates Gmsh 2D geometry for directly bounded planar regions, external-flow obstacle domains, and internal-flow channels.
principle: STL facets carry coordinates and triangle topology, not standard CFD boundary-condition semantics. Singly incident triangle edges reconstruct the body loop. A sidecar either assigns names to a planar region boundary or defines a rectangular external-flow domain whose four sides are Inlet, Outlet, Symmetry and Farfield and whose internal STL loop is Wall. Physical names require a separate mapping to OneFLOW BC semantics. External flow constructs a fluid surface by subtracting an internal obstacle loop from an enclosing outer loop; internal flow uses the STL boundary loop itself as the closed fluid-domain boundary. Both assign physical names independently of solver boundary-state configuration.
architecture: Native C++: STL -> StlMeshReader -> tolerance-based vertex welding and single planar boundary loop -> explicit Case layout JSON -> Gmsh .geo -> configured Gmsh CLI -> MSH 4.1 -> existing C++ Gmsh reader and topology/Physical Group validation. Independent Python reference Cases use grid/stl/stl_to_gmsh.py. The existing external-flow Python preprocessing Case at grid/stl_to_gmsh/script/run.py with config/external_flow.json remains a separate mode. The square_2x2 native Case reuses the exact square STL and changes only its transfinite layout. An optional development dependency graph reuses the Workbench planner and runner to stage STL -> Gmsh -> CGNS -> OneFLOW -> CFD Cases, validate MSH 4.1 topology and physical names, and retain per-stage logs and runtime environment evidence outside the source tree.

proves: ASCII and binary STL triangle records can be read and a planar square fixture yields one four-edge boundary loop.
The planar STL loop can be used as an internal wall hole inside an explicitly bounded rectangular fluid domain.
The four outer rectangle sides and internal wall are emitted as separate named Gmsh Physical Curve groups.
The native C++ Grid conversion route accepts STL as source and Gmsh as target for a single axis-aligned rectangular XY boundary with explicit transfinite cell counts.
The native C++ route validates generated MSH 4.1 node counts, LINE_2 and QUAD_4 element counts, and the four outer Physical Curve names plus fluid_domain.
The square and two_square_cells native C++ Cases and their independent Python references are registered separately in the grid Case catalog.
The square_2x2 native Case reuses the square STL geometry and changes only the transfinite layout to produce a 2 x 2 quadrilateral mesh.
The STL-to-CFD workflow declares explicit artifact handoffs through Gmsh MSH 4.1, CGNS, a native OneFLOW grid, and a CFD Solve Case, using isolated run directories.
The Python external-flow reference Case builds a rectangular fluid domain with a polygonal STL obstacle as a named internal Wall boundary.
The Python internal-flow reference Case uses a closed rectangular STL loop as the fluid-domain boundary and emits named inlet, outlet and wall Physical Curves.
The channel reference Case generates a deterministic 20 x 5 transfinite quadrilateral mesh, while the unstructured external-flow Case validates minimum mesh counts and exact Physical Group names.
The native C++ STL-to-Gmsh Case builds a 2D external-flow fluid domain by enclosing a planar STL body loop in a rectangular outer domain and creating a Plane Surface with the body as a hole.
The native C++ and Python circle external-flow Cases use byte-identical STL input and matching domain bounds, mesh-size controls and Physical Group names.

The native circle external-flow Case is registered for both Run Development Cases and Mesh-to-CFD Validation; the latter executes the selected MSH through the existing CGNS, OneFLOW-grid and CFD smoke-test chain.
does_not_prove: Generated outer-flow meshes have been converted through CGNS into a OneFLOW native grid.

Gmsh Physical Curve names have been converted into solver boundary-condition state values.
